name: nlp_gpt_pretrain
title: A nanoGPT-shaped from-scratch pre-training loop: gradient accumulation, a cosine schedule, AMP, torch.compile and a checkpoint resume
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the LLM-from-scratch shape
note: MLV207 and MLV208 miss for one shared reason: build() returns (model, optimizer, scheduler, scaler) as a tuple, and a receiver that arrives through a helper's return keeps its family but loses the constructor MLV207/MLV208 read. Rewriting build() inline makes both fire (finding NLP-05).

expected.why: nn.Module's parameter registry is never built, so self.qkv and self.proj are not returned by parameters() and the attention blocks are never optimised

expected.defect: the transformer stack is a plain list comprehension, not an nn.ModuleList
expected.why: none of the six blocks is registered, so AdamW(model.parameters()) optimises the embeddings and the head only and the model trains to a bag-of-words

expected.defect: the head applies F.softmax before the cross-entropy loss
expected.why: cross_entropy applies log_softmax itself, so the gradient is computed through a double softmax and the model learns far slower than the loss curve suggests

expected.defect: the gradient clip runs at the top of the step, before backward()
expected.why: it clips whatever gradients survived the previous iteration, so the clip that is supposed to stop the loss spiking never sees the gradients it is meant to bound

expected.defect: CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=EPOCHS) is stepped once per batch
expected.why: the cosine completes its whole decay inside the first epoch's first two batches and the rest of the run trains at the floor learning rate - silently, because nothing raises

expected.defect: with a GradScaler in use the loop calls optimizer.step() instead of scaler.step(optimizer), and never unscales
expected.why: the scaled gradients are applied as if they were real ones, so the effective learning rate is multiplied by the scale factor and the run diverges on the first inf check

expected.defect: the running loss accumulates the tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: every iteration's autograd graph is kept alive for the whole epoch, which is an out-of-memory on a long pre-training run and nothing else

expected.defect: the resume path calls torch.load with neither weights_only= nor map_location=
expected.why: it unpickles arbitrary objects and fails on a machine without the device the checkpoint was written on

expected.defect: the whole compiled module is pickled rather than model.state_dict()
expected.why: a torch.compile()d module pickles its wrapper, so the checkpoint does not reload into an uncompiled model at all
the initialisation and the shuffled batch order both move between runs, so two pre-training curves cannot be compared

forbidden.why: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called on line 67 inside the `if (step + 1) % ACCUM_STEPS == 0` accumulation guard, which is the correct gradient-accumulation shape and the exact false-positive trap MLV201's note (a) names
optimizer.step() is called on line 65, inside the same accumulation guard
there is no torch.no_grad() block in this project; torch.autocast is not a no-grad context
the training loader passes shuffle=True on line 29
there is no evaluation loader in this project at all
the DataLoader takes no num_workers=, so the spawn footgun does not apply
there is no evaluation pass in this project - the defect is that it never evaluates, not that it evaluates wrongly
same - no evaluation region exists here
inputs and targets are both moved with .to(device) on lines 57-58, before the forward on line 61
self.mlp is an nn.Sequential, which registers its children - the container MLV702 asks for
there is no split call in this project; the token stream is one contiguous corpus

unsupported.defect: the causal mask is allocated on the default device inside forward(), so on CUDA it is built on the CPU on every forward and either raises or silently synchronises
unsupported.why: MLV503 (tensor allocated inside the batch loop without device=) is a later-tier rule and is not built

unsupported.defect: resume() is defined and never called, so the checkpoint main() writes is never read back and a restarted run silently begins from scratch
unsupported.why: MLV802's not_restored variant is a later-tier rule and is not built; MLV903 (orphan stage) is also later-tier

unsupported.defect: total_loss is never reset between epochs, so the printed mean loss is a running mean over the whole run and looks like it is still improving after it has plateaued
unsupported.why: no rule models an accumulator's reset cadence
